knackRulesIntro: Schwimmen uses a 32-card deck from seven through ace and is played by two to six people. This implementation uses the common layout with three face-up center cards.
knackRulesGoalBody: Make the highest possible value with your three cards. Only the best total in one suit counts. The lowest value at the end of a round loses a life.
knackRules_setupBody: Everyone receives three private cards. Three more cards lie face up in the center, and the remaining stock stays face down.
knackRules_scoreBody: An ace is eleven; kings, queens, jacks, and tens are ten; number cards use their face value. Only cards of one suit are added. Three equal ranks score 30.5. Three aces are Fire, the top combination; an ace plus two ten-value cards of one suit makes 31.
knackRules_turnBody: On your turn, exchange exactly one hand card for exactly one center card, or exchange all three hand cards for all three center cards. You may never exchange exactly two cards.
knackRules_passBody: You may pass instead of exchanging. If every active player passes consecutively, the three center cards are discarded and replaced from the stock. If fewer than three remain, the round is scored.
knackRules_knockBody: You may knock instead of exchanging. Every other active player then receives exactly one final turn before scoring; the player who knocked does not play again.
knackRules_roundBody: A 31 or Fire ends the round immediately. Fire makes every other active player lose one life. Otherwise, everyone tied for the lowest score loses a life.
knackRules_livesBody: Everyone begins with three lives. After losing the last life, a player is swimming and remains in the game. Their next loss eliminates them.
knackRulesEndBody: The last player who has not been eliminated wins.

mauMauRulesIntro: Mau-Mau uses a 32-card deck from seven through ace and is played by two to six people.
mauMauRulesGoalBody: Be the first to discard all five cards in your hand. The suit and rank of the top discard determine which card can follow.
mauMauRules_setupBody: Everyone receives five cards. A normal card without a special effect starts the face-up discard pile, and the remaining cards form the face-down stock.
mauMauRules_playBody: Play exactly one card whose suit or rank matches the top discard. A jack is the exception and always fits. Play then normally passes clockwise.
mauMauRules_drawBody: If no card in your hand fits, draw exactly one. If it fits, you may play it immediately or keep it. If it does not fit, your turn ends automatically.
mauMauRules_sevenBody: After a seven, the next player draws two cards and is skipped.
mauMauRules_eightBody: After an eight, the next player is skipped. In a two-player game, this gives the same player another turn.
mauMauRules_jackBody: A jack can be played on any card. When playing it, choose clubs, diamonds, hearts, or spades; the next play must match that suit.
mauMauRules_stockBody: When the stock is empty, the top discard remains in place. All older discards are shuffled to form a new stock.
mauMauRulesEndBody: The first player to play their final card legally wins immediately.
rulesIntro: Podkidnoy Durak is played by two to six people. There are no teams: everyone tries to get rid of their own cards before the others.
rulesGoalBody: Once the draw pile is empty, players who have no cards left finish successfully. The only person still holding cards at the end is the Durak and loses.
rules_setupBody: Each player receives six cards. A card at the draw pile determines the trump suit. The player holding the lowest trump makes the first attack.
rules_attackBody: The attacker places any card or several cards of the same rank from their hand face up on the table. The next active player in seating order is the defender.
rules_defenseBody: The defender must beat every attack separately, either with a higher card of the same suit or with a trump. A trump can only be beaten by a higher trump.
rules_throwInBody: After all open attacks have been covered, the attackers may throw in cards in turn. Every new card's rank must already appear on the table. A round allows no more than six attack cards and never more than the defender held at its start.
rules_takeBody: If the defender cannot or does not want to cover everything, they choose “Pick up cards”. The round ends immediately and the defender takes every attack and defense card into their hand; no more cards may be thrown in.
rules_roundEndBody: If every card was covered and all attackers pass, the table cards leave the game and the previous defender attacks next. After a pickup, the defender is skipped. Starting with the original attacker, players draw back up to six cards; the defender draws last.
rulesGameEndBody: Once the pile is exhausted, no more cards are drawn. A player with no cards is finished. The last person holding cards loses as the Durak. If all remaining players discard their final cards together, the game ends in a draw.
